chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Hamza, from Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, who said:

I asked Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him): 'How old was Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) on the day he became a Muslim?' He said: 'Was he ever an infidel? Rather, when Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sent His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), Ali was ten years old, and he was not an infidel on that day. He had believed in Allah and His Messenger, and he preceded all people in faith in Allah and His Messenger, and in Prayer by three years.'

The first prayer he prayed with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was Dhuhr, two cycles. Thus, Allah, the Blessed and High, obligated it upon whoever became a Muslim in Mecca as two cycles, two cycles. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prayed it in Mecca as two cycles, and Ali (peace be upon him) prayed it with him in Mecca as two cycles for a period of ten years, until the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) migrated to Medina and left Ali (peace be upon him) behind regarding matters that no one else could handle.

The departure of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) from Mecca was on the first day of Rabi' al-Awwal, which was Thursday of the thirteenth year from the Prophethood. He arrived in Medina after twelve nights had passed from the month of Rabi' al-Awwal, with the setting of the sun. So he descended at Quba, prayed Dhuhr two cycles and Asr two cycles. Then he did not cease to stay there, awaiting Ali (peace be upon him), praying the five prayers as two cycles, two cycles.

He stayed at the house of Amr ibn Awf, and remained with them for about ten days. They would say to him: 'Will you stay with us so we may build for you a house and a mosque?' He would say: 'No, I am awaiting Ali ibn Abi Talib, and I have ordered him to join me. I will not settle in a house until Ali arrives, and he will not be long, if Allah wills.' So Ali (peace be upon him) arrived while the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was in the house of Amr ibn Awf, and he stayed with him.

Then, when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) received Ali (peace be upon him), he moved from Quba to Banu Salim ibn Awf, with Ali (peace be upon him) with him on Friday at sunrise. So they drew a boundary for him for a mosque and established its Qibla. He prayed with them in it the Friday prayer of two cycles and preached two sermons. Then he returned that same day to Medina on the she-camel upon which he had arrived, with Ali (peace be upon him) with him, not separating from him, walking with his walk.

And whenever the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) passed by a valley from the valleys of the Ansar, they would stand up for him, asking him to descend upon them. He would say to them: 'Make way for the she-camel, for it is under instruction.' So it went with him, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was holding its reins, until it reached the place which you see. He gestured with his hand to the door of the mosque of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) by which funeral prayers are performed. So it stopped at it, knelt, and placed its humps on the ground.

So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) descended, and Abu Ayyub hastened, carrying his saddle, and brought him into his house. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and Ali (peace be upon him) stayed with him until his mosque was built for him, his houses were built for him, and the house of Ali (peace be upon him) was built. So they two moved to their houses.

Saeed ibn al-Musayyab said to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him): 'May I be sacrificed for you, Abu Bakr was with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) when he arrived in Medina. So when did he separate from him?' He said: 'When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) arrived at Quba, he stayed with them awaiting the arrival of Ali (peace be upon him). Abu Bakr said to him: 'Rise with us to Medina, for the people have rejoiced at your arrival and are eager for your coming to them. So go with us and do not stay here awaiting Ali, for I do not think he will arrive to you for a month.'

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'No, he will not be long. I will not move until my cousin and my brother in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and the most beloved of my family to me arrives, for he saved me with his own self from the polytheists.' He said: 'At that, Abu Bakr became angry and was disgusted, and envy for Ali (peace be upon him) entered him. And that was the first enmity that appeared from him towards the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) regarding Ali (peace be upon him), and the first opposition to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). So he went until he entered Medina, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) remained at Quba awaiting Ali (peace be upon him).'

He said: 'I said to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him): 'When did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) marry Fatima to Ali (peace be upon him)?' He said: 'In Medina, one year after the Migration, and she was nine years old on that day.' Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'And no one was born to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) from Khadija (peace be upon her) upon the nature of Islam except Fatima (peace be upon her). And Khadija died one year before the Migration, and Abu Talib died one year after the death of Khadija.'

When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) lost them, he grew tired of staying in Mecca, and intense grief entered him, and he feared for himself from the disbelievers of Quraysh. So he complained of that to Jibreel (peace be upon him), and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: 'Go out from the town whose people are unjust, and migrate to Medina, for today you have no helper in Mecca, and declare war against the polytheists.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) directed himself to Medina.

I said to him: 'When was the Prayer made obligatory upon the Muslims in the form that they are upon today?' He said: 'In Medina, when the call became apparent and Islam strengthened, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, decreed Jihad upon the Muslims. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) added seven cycles to the Prayer: two cycles in Dhuhr, two cycles in Asr, one cycle in Maghrib, and two cycles in the last Isha, and he confirmed Fajr upon what it was obligated in.'

To hasten the descent of the angels of the day from the sky, and to hasten the ascent of the angels of the night to the sky. And the angels of the night and the angels of the day would testify with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) for the Prayer of Fajr. Therefore, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'And the Quran of dawn. Indeed, the Quran of dawn is witnessed.' Witnessed by the Muslims, and witnessed by the angels of the day and the angels of the night.

key_terms.رَبِيعٍ الْأَوَّلِ: Rabi' al-Awwal (the third month of the Islamic calendar)
key_terms.قُبَا: Quba (a suburb of Medina where the Prophet first stayed)

ai.seo_question: How old was Ali when he became a Muslim and when were the five daily prayers established?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi establishes the Shia doctrine of 'Alam al-Ali' (Ali's early, continuous faith) by asserting he was never a disbeliever and was the first to pray with the Prophet, serving as a counter-narrative to Sunni claims of Abu Bakr's primacy. It further details the historical timeline of the Hijra, noting the Prophet's deliberate delay in entering Medina until Ali joined him, and explains the theological rationale for the Fajr prayer's timing as a witness to the transition of angels. The text concludes by linking the establishment of the five daily prayers to the period of strengthened Islamic authority in Medina.

en.hubeali: H 14983 – Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Abu Hamza, from Saeed Bin Al-Musayyab who said: I asked Aliasws Bin Al-Husaynasws, ‘How old was Aliasws on the day heasws became a Muslim?’ So heasws said: ‘What? Was heasws an infidel ever? But rather, when Allahazwj Sent Hisazwj Messengersaww, Aliasws was ten years old, and heasws was never an infidel on that day, and heasws had believed in Allahazwj, and in Hisazwj Messengersaww, and preceded all of the people to the faith by Allahazwj and by Hisazwj Messengersaww and to the Prayer by three years’. And the first Prayer that heasws Prayed with the Rasool Allahsaww was Al-Zohr (Midday) of two cycles and that is what Allahazwj Blessed and High had Obligated it as upon the one who became a Muslim at Makkah – two cycles, two cycles, and the Rasool Allahsaww had Prayed two cycles at Makkah, and Aliasws had Prayed it with himsaww as two cycles for a period of ten years until the Rasool Allahsaww migrated to Al-Medina, and left Aliasws behind regarding the matters which no one part from himasws could have dealt with. And the going out of the Rasool Allahsaww from Makkah was during the first of the Rabbi-ul-Awwal, and that was the day of Thursday on the thirteenth year from the Mab’as (Declaration of Prophet-hood), and journeyed to Al-Medina over twelve nights from the Month of Rabbi Ul-Awwal with the setting of the sun. So hesaww descended at Quba, so hesaww Prayed Al-Zohr two cycles, and Al-Asr two cycles. Then hesaww did not cease to stay there, awaiting Aliasws. Hesaww Prayed five Prayers of two cycles, two cycles. And hesaww stayed at (the house of) Amro Bin Awf for about ten days. They were saying to himsaww, ‘Stay with us, so we will build for yousaww house and a Masjid’. So hesaww said; ‘No. Isaww am awaiting Aliasws Bin Abu Talibasws, and have ordered himasws to meet mesaww, and will not settle in a house until Aliasws comes, and heasws will not be long, Allahazwj Willing. So Aliasws came to the Prophetsaww at the house of Amro Bin Awf and stayed with himsaww. Then the Rasool Allahsaww, when Aliasws arrived to himsaww, transferred from Quba to the Clan of Saalim Bin Awf, and Aliasws was with himsaww, on the Day of Friday at sunrise. So they drew a boundary for himsaww for a Masjid, and established its Qiblah (direction of Prayer). Hesaww Prayed with them the Friday Prayer of two cycles, and preached them two sermons. Then hesaww went to Al-Medina upon the she-camel which hesaww had come upon, and Aliasws was with himsaww, not separating from himsaww, walking with himsaww step by step. And there was no neighbourhood from the neighbourhoods of the Helpers which Rasool Allahsaww passed by except that they stood up for himsaww asking himsaww to descend to them. Hesaww would say to them; ‘Make way for the she-camel for it is under instructions (of where to go). So it went and the Rasool Allahsaww had freed its reins until it ended up at the place which you see’, and heasws gestured by hisasws hands to the door of the Masjid of the Rasool Allahsaww by which the funeral Prayers are performed. Heasws said: ‘So it paused at it and knelt, and placed itself upon the ground. So the Rasool Allahsaww descended, and Abu Ayub welcomed himsaww to the extent that he carried hissaww saddle bag and made himsaww to enter his house. And the Rasool Allahsaww and Aliasws stayed with him until they built for himsaww, hissaww Masjid, and built for himsaww hissaww house, and a house for Aliasws. So they two of themasws transferred to theirasws houses’. So Saeed Bin Al-Musayyab (the narrator) said to Aliasws Bin Al-Husaynasws, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws, Abu Bakr was with the Rasool Allahsaww when hesaww arrived at Al-Medina. So when did he separate from himsaww?’ So heasws said: ‘Abu Bakr was with himsaww when the Rasool Allahsaww proceeded to Quba, and hesaww decided to wait for Aliasws. So Abu Bakr said to himsaww, ‘Come with us to Al-Medina, for the people would rejoice at yoursaww arrival there and are eager to welcome yousaww. So come with us and do not stay over here waiting for Aliasws, from what I can see, it would take himasws a month to come to youasws’. So the Rasool Allahsaww said to him: ‘Never! Heasws will not be long, and Isaww will not move until mysaww cousinasws, and mysaww brotherasws for the sake of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic, and the most beloved to mesaww of mysaww Family comes over, for heasws saved mesaww from the Polytheists by being in mysaww place’. Heasws said; ‘So Abu Bakr was angry and was disgusted by it, and envy for Aliasws entered into him due to that, and that was the first enmity initiated from him to the Rasool Allahsaww with regards to Aliasws, and the first of his opposition to the Rasool Allahsaww. So he went until he entered Al-Medina, and left behind the Rasool Allahsaww at Quba waiting for Aliasws’. (The narrator) said, ‘I said to Aliasws Bin Al-Husaynasws, ‘So when did the Messengersaww get Fatimaasws married to Aliasws?’ Heasws said: ‘At Al-Medina, a year after the Migration, and she was in herasws ninth year’. Aliasws Bin Al-Husaynasws said: ‘And there was no birth to the Rasool Allahsaww from Khadijaas upon the nature of Al-Islam except for Fatimaasws, and Khadijaas had passed away a year before the Migration, and Abu Talibas had passed away a year after heras passing away. So when the two of themas passed away, the Rasool Allahsaww got tired of staying at Makkah, and was overcome by intense grief and sympathised with himselfsaww from the infidels of Qureysh. Hesaww informed Jibraeelas about that, so Allahazwj Revealed unto himsaww: “Go out from the town where (its) people are unjust and Migrate to Al-Medina, for today there is no helper for yousaww at Makkah, and establish a war against the Polytheists”. So the Rasool Allahsaww heeded that and directed himselfsaww to Al-Medina’. So I (the narrator) said to himasws, ‘So when was the Salat became Obligatory upon the Muslims in the form that they are Praying today?’ Heasws said: ‘At Al-Medina when the Call was made apparent, and Al-Islam was strong, and Allahazwj Decreed Al-Jihaad upon the Muslims, and the Rasool Allahsaww increased in the Prayer, seven cycles – two cycles in Al-Zohr, and two cycles in Al-Asr, and one cycle in Al-Maghrib, and two cycles in Al-Isha, and accepted Al-Fajr upon what it had been Obligated in order to expedite the descent of the Angels of the day from the sky and to expedite that rising of the Angels of the night to the sky. And the Angels of the night and the Angels of the day had been testifying with the Rasool Allahsaww for Al-Fajr Prayer, so that is the Statement of Allahazwj: “[17:78] (the recital of) the Qur'an at dawn. Lo! (the recital of) the Qur'an at dawn is witnessed”, witnessed by the Muslims and witnessed by the Angels of the day and Angels of the night’.
en.sarwar: 537. Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, who has narrated the following:
Abu Abdullah (a.s.) has said: ‘How easy it is to make the people to be happy with you. Just restrain your tongues from (speaking against) them’.
